text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zambian press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The public sector reform programme is set to move into top gear with over 3,000 civil servants expected to be retrenched this year.
- Zaire has assured Zambia that it will take disciplinary action against Zairean diplomats involved in smuggling.
- Illegal vendors in the Zambian capital have asked the government to extend a one-week ultimatum to leave the city centre so they can reorganise themselves.
- Zaire, responding to allegations that its diplomats in Zambia are involved in smuggling, said cross-border crimes are committed by nationals from both countries.
- The State had intensified its hunt for witnesses in a court electoral petition challenging President Frederick Chiluba's election victory last year.
- Workers at the closed Mansa Batteries plant say they will auction the company's assets if management fails to pay out benefits within 10 days.
